h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, י׳ Ki Seitzei, 10
The Barren Tziyon Brings Forth Precious Souls

p: and it corresponds to the fifth attribute
which is the attribute of Hod;
and corresponding to it is the fifth day
of the seven days of Creation.
And on this day there took place
and the blessing of the fish,
in whom there is very great increase,
for they are hidden from the eye,
only in a thing hidden from the eye.
"And may they multiply like fish, abundantly":
"Just as with fish in the sea,
If you are a numerous people,
"go and hide yourselves in the forests,
so that the evil eye have no power over you";
the evil eye has no power"
וּכְשֶׁבֵּירַךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל (דְּבָרִים א, יא)
And when Moshe Rabbeinu blessed Yisrael (Devarim 1:11):
"May He add to you as many as you are
it says (Midrash Rabbah, Parshas Devarim; Devarim Rabbah 1:13):
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֹא נָתַן קִצְבָה
the Holy One, Blessed is He, set no limit
and you said a thousand times?'
when the Holy One, Blessed is He, comes,
as He has spoken to you.'"
Now the blessing of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
also comes to an enormous figure,
a thousand times six hundred thousand,
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בִּרְכָתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and all the more so the blessing of Hashem Yisbarach,
yet we do not find that it was fulfilled
except in the days of Shlomo,
כַּחוֹל אֲשֶׁר עַל הַיָּם לָרוֹב וְגוֹ׳
as the sand that is by the sea in multitude," etc.;
that then they were without limit.
Also, according to what they said (Eichah Rabbah 1:2),
the reckoning that there were in Yerushalayim
twice as many as those who left Egypt,"
this too comes to a vast number.
no such increase is found in Yisrael,
אַף כְּבִרְכַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
not even as in the blessing of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
not as in the blessing of Hashem Yisbarach.
It turns out that Knesses Yisrael resembles a barren woman,
and they are pained: where are the blessings?
And corresponding to this attribute comes
"Sing, O barren one, who did not bear," etc.
And they said in the Gemara (Berachos 10a):
who has not borne children for Gehinnom
which implies that her resembling a barren woman
is what causes worthy children to come forth.
And this follows what is counted
in the new Pesikta (Pesikta deRav Kahana 20:1):
even given the greatness of their level,
nevertheless, when they had to give birth to
as Yitzchak and Yaakov and the Shevatim,
And regarding Yitzchak we find explicitly
"I shall establish cinnamon in the world, etc.;
so too, once his blood is bound up, etc.,
once his desire is spent, etc."
dross still came forth from Yitzchak;
all the more so when there were to be born
And so too the wife of Manoach,
who was to give birth to Shimshon,
שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא וְכוּלֵּי
of the Holy One, Blessed is He," etc.
only he still needed further refinements.
for he would be a nazir;
and once they shaved his nazirite locks,
And so Channah, the mother of Shmuel,
who was the master of all the prophets
for Moshe Rabbeinu was a chariot
and Aharon for the attribute of Hod,
the glass that does not shine,
and Shmuel is equal to Moshe and Aharon,
so that she would bear a soul as precious as Shmuel.
which is the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג לה, א)
as is written in the holy Zohar (III 35a):
is called by the name Tziyon,
in order to bring forth precious souls.
"Sing, O barren one, who did not bear"
over the very fact that she did not bear;
over the very fact that she did not travail;
"for more are the children of the desolate one
than the children of the married one."
And in the Pesikta (Pesikta deRav Kahana 20:5):
"'For more are the children of the desolate one,' etc.:
she raised up for Me more righteous men in her destruction
she raised up for Me when she was built."
about increase in number, in quantity,
is also about increase in quality:
are the children of the desolate one than the children of the married one.
And therefore, so that there come forth
which is Knesses Yisrael, had to be
